transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squealing noise that lasts a few minutes then fades is very often caused by the jockey (idler) pulley or the drive belt. These parts can glaze or stiffen when cold, causing a high-pitched squeal until they warm up and spin freely again. Another possibility is a small object like a coin or key trapped between the drum and the tub, which might shift as it spins. To help narrow this down, please unplug the machine first, then try turning the drum by hand to see if it feels rough or makes noise. Also, check inside the drum and behind the lint filter for any foreign objects.
Unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns but there's a slight squeak/scrape and feels a bit rough. Nothing stuck in the door seal or filter area that I can see.

Since the drum turns but feels rough with a squeak, and nothing is stuck in the drum, this points strongly to the drive system components rather than an obstruction. The most likely cause is the jockey (idler) pulley bearing wearing out; it creates friction when cold that eases as it warms up. A stiff or glazed belt could also be causing this. To confirm which part is failing, you need to inspect the pulley directly. Please open the front panel (typically by removing the lint filter housing or two screws at the top corners) and locate the small spring-loaded idler pulley pressing against the belt. Spin it by hand: if it feels gritty, resists turning, or squeaks, that is the faulty part.
I'm not sure how to get the front panel off on this one, and I've only got basic tools. I also can't tilt or lift it because of my back. Is there anything else I can check without taking it apart?

Since you can't open the panel or tilt it, we have to rely on listening. With the dryer unplugged and empty, press your ear close to the front grille (where the lint filter is) and turn the drum slowly by hand again. If you hear a distinct gritty grinding or squeaking coming from that specific area as the drum turns, it suggests the jockey pulley bearing inside is failing. This part wears out over time and needs replacing, which requires taking the machine apart. Given your back issues and lack of tools, I recommend calling an engineer to check the idler pulley.

candidates: Jockey/idler pulley or drive belt wear (high)
Foreign object trapped in drum or filter housing (medium)
Drum support rollers or bearing wear (low)
